answer: To defeat Sybil attacks, agents must bind identities to a cryptographic stake burning mechanism. Each new agent node acts like a growing vine in a trust graph, using a provable burned-capital receipt as its root anchor. To register k identities, quadratic slash penalties and exponential proof-of-burn curves force attacker costs to scale superlinearly as O(k^2). A failure or malicious ripple triggers collateral destruction across neighbor links, making identity cloning economically irrational.
